correctness.rationale: The output-comparison identity is proved for arbitrary words and every exact burst length. A two-distance graph decomposes at size a+b into gcd(a,b) cycles, producing an exact forest-to-cycle cutoff and a cycle-rank formula. The joint-minimum event proves necessity of the independence threshold independently of zero covariance. Centered edge products vanish on forests; additive length triples are precisely the 3-edge triangles, counted exactly. Each triangle contributes -(q-1)/q^3. Full direct-descendant enumeration in 19 alphabet/length cases checks identities and boundaries with exact rational arithmetic; the infinite result rests on the proof, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: Published single-burst formulas give each marginal separately. Direct scientific implication comparison shows they do not determine the exact independence boundary of two ball-size variables, its gcd-governed joint-minimum ratio, or the additive support and magnitude of three distinct-length centered moments. Relevant 2016 and 2022 full-text sections and appendices were inspected, and targeted research-record/literature searches found no covering stronger statement. This is a same-model best-knowledge assessment, not uniqueness certification.
residual_risks: An unindexed graph-coloring or random-lag-mismatch theorem under non-coding terminology may imply the result.
Original Levenshtein 1967 paper was cited through the 2016 full text rather than inspected in its original language.
No independent expert or external originality audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies an exact, nontrivial gcd-governed phase boundary for independence of competing fixed-length burst deletion-ball sizes, a closed-form minimum-event dependence ratio, and additive third-order interactions despite pairwise zero covariance. These address natural multi-burst-channel sphere statistics and prevent treating marginal volume laws as jointly independent. None is merely a recount of the known single-burst distribution. Scope and model limitations are explicit.
